scenes.narration: The private years of Mirek Topolánek explain the public decades better than any speech. Between 2006 and 2009, Topolánek was the member of the Chamber of Deputies (MP) and senator from Ostrava from 1996 until 2004. After leaving politics in 2010, Topolánek has been active in the electric power industry as a vocal lobbyist for the fossil fuel industry.

The family Mirek Topolánek came from matters more than the legends admit. On 24 March 2009, Topolánek resigned as prime minister after he lost a no-confidence vote in the Chamber of Deputies. He remained in office until 8 May, at which point Jan Fischer took office as an independent prime minister leading an interim caretaker government.

The first real success of Mirek Topolánek arrived later than anyone expected, and changed everything. In November 2017, Topolánek announced his bid for the presidency in the 2018 election but received only 4% and came sixth in the election. Mirek Topolánek attended a military high school in Opava, where he became a Socialistic Union of Youth member which he claimed to be semi-obligatory for future career officers of the Czechoslovak People's Army.

The last chapter of Mirek Topolánek was written long after the fame. After finishing he studied at Brno University of Technology where he received an Ing. degree in mechanical engineering. In 1996 he won a scholarship for Training Course in Management of small and medium enterprise (MIM) in Cyprus and also attended a post-graduate Course in Corporate Management (Centre for Management Training, Čelákovice CZ).

The whole life of Mirek Topolánek reads like a single decision repeated. He entered politics by becoming a member of a post-communist catch-all civic movement Civic Forum in 1989 and has been a member of the Civic Democratic Party since 1994. Topolánek co-founded the engineering company VAE Ltd. in 1991 and was a member of the VAE Inc. board of directors from 1996 to 2003.

Between the birth and the legend of Mirek Topolánek lie the years that actually decide it. Topolánek ran in the 1996 Senate election in Ostrava-city district where he faced the Social Democrat candidate Jiří Smejkal. His campaign drew the attention of media due to its being largely focused on Topolánek's family, which was at the time considered unusual in the Czech Republic.

The reputation of Mirek Topolánek was built in the middle, not at the edges. Topolánek won the election when, defeating his rival by a margin of 630 votes and becoming the new Senator. Topolánek was elected in leader of leader of Ostravan regional organisation of ODS in 1998 by large margin.

Somebody like Mirek Topolánek should not have made it — that is exactly why the story survives. Topolánek did not seek a third term in Senate during 2004 election. After being elected the leader of the Civic Democratic Party in 2002 Topolánek participated in the 2006 legislative election which produced a hung parliament (100 seats for left-leaning and 100 for right-leaning parties out of 200 Chamber of Deputies members).

The life of Mirek Topolánek begins far from where the story usually starts. Topolánek was appointed prime minister by President Václav Klaus on 16 August 2006 and introduced a unicolour government (nine members of the Civic Democratic Party and six independents). The cabinet failed to gain confidence in the Chamber of Deputies, but he continued to be caretaker prime minister until 9 January 2007, when his second cabinet was appointed.

Mirek Topolánek was not born famous — the early years shaped everything that followed. He put together a centre-right coalition government with the Green Party and Christian and Democratic Union – Czechoslovak People's Party. It finally gained confidence on 19 January 2007 (230 days after the elections), thanks to two social democratic MPs who abstained, thus effectively defaulting to a right-wing government rather than the unstable situation ongoing since June 2006.

To understand where Mirek Topolánek ended up, start with where Mirek Topolánek began. Topolánek then negotiated coalition with Christian and Democratic Union – Czechoslovak People's Party and Green Party. On 19 January 2007, Chamber of Deputies passed the government's confidence vote with 100 MPs voting in favour, while 97 MPs voted against.

The road from the beginning to the peak of Mirek Topolánek ran through years nobody filmed. Mirek Topolánek introduced the so-called "Five Prime Minister's Priorities" in October 2007. It was a government statement which includes 10 program areas, which consist of 190 projects of Government's Program Goals Through Electoral Term accepted by the government.

Each stage of the life of Mirek Topolánek made the next stage possible. To facilitate orientation and communication with citizens Mirek Topolánek had summarised the 10 program areas to Five Prime Minister's Priorities: Healthy Public Finances, Modern and Efficient State, Safe Citizen in a Safe Country, Removing Barriers, Promoting Science and Education. Topolánek's government led the Czech Republic during Czech Presidency of the Council of the European Union in 2009.

The people who knew Mirek Topolánek young describe someone already restless. Topolánek and his team was able to negotiate a compromise between Russia and Ukraine. Topolánek remained in position of President of European Council until his government was replaced by Jan Fischer's Cabinet.

What Mirek Topolánek built in the middle years is what the name still stands for. On 24 March 2009, after four failed earlier attempts, the opposition ČSSD and communists party succeeded in leading the lower house of the Czech parliament to a no confidence vote in Topolánek's government. The measure passed with 101 votes to 96 as four members of Topolánek's coalition (two of his own party) voting with the opposition.

By the time Mirek Topolánek reached the defining moment, the preparation was decades old. After the vote, Topolánek said that he would resign in accordance with the Constitution. He confidently said: "We believe the president should also follow the custom and appoint me to form a new government." Although surprised by the vote, the European Commission stated that it had confidence in the Czech Republic, and that the nation's EU presidency would remain unaffected.

The rise of Mirek Topolánek was not an accident — in retrospect the pattern is plain. On 15 September 2009, Topolánek resigned his seat in the Chamber of Deputies after ČSSD announced a delay of proposed snap election in October 2009. Topolánek has been criticised for his rhetoric, which occasionally invokes memories of the World War II and Nazi atrocities.

Setbacks came early for Mirek Topolánek, and the response to them is the real story. In August 2003 Topolánek called the programme of the competing Social Democratic Party (ČSSD) to be a "osvětimská lež" (Auschwitz lie), a common expression in Czech which denotes Holocaust denial. This was used in the 1930s by the Sudetendeutsche Party representing Germans in the former Czechoslovakia, and meant that the day will come, when the Sudeten Area will become a part of Germany.

The legacy of Mirek Topolánek outlived the circumstances that produced it. Also in 2007, Topolánek was criticised when he raised his middle finger in the lower house. In October 2008, Topolánek lashed out at a photographer who was taking photographs of his 15-month-old son.

Few lives travel as far as that of Mirek Topolánek, and the distance is the point. BBC reported that at one stage Topolánek pushed the photographer against a wall and threateningly asked why he was taking photos of him. On 30 May 2009, the Italian police seized photos under suspicion of a violation of privacy.

The childhood of Mirek Topolánek contains the adult in small print. One photo, according to world media showed Topolánek naked at Villa Certosa (Silvio Berlusconi's summer house) in May 2008. In the end, Topolánek admitted the naked man sunbathing near a topless women in Berlusconi's Villa Certosa was himself.

Money, luck and timing all played their parts in the life of Mirek Topolánek — in that order. He also expressed his contempt towards voters of ČSSD and described their view on minorities as 'imprison them all and kick up their arses'. He did apologize for his statements, which he claimed were taken out of context, on 21 March 2010.

The turning point in the life of Mirek Topolánek looked like a failure at the time. Prime Minister Fischer replied to Topolánek's statements describing them as 'stupid, insulting and misleading'. In the light of this controversy, Topolánek decided to step down as election leader of Civic Democratic Party in the May 2010 legislative election.

Every biography of Mirek Topolánek has to pass through the years that were quietly lost. In April 2015 he was expelled from ODS for failing to pay a members' fee. His business focuses on consultancy, mediation of business and services, real estate activities, real estate management and maintenance, development and development of technical designs, research and development, advertising and marketing and media representation.

The education of Mirek Topolánek happened mostly outside any school. Topolánek himself admitted that contacts he made in politics helped him to succeed in business. On 3 November 2017, Václav Klaus Jr. stated that Topolánek was seeking nomination of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS) for the 2018 presidential election.

What Mirek Topolánek wanted at the start and what Mirek Topolánek got are not the same thing, and that gap is the story. Topolánek discussed his candidacy with party's leader Petr Fiala and asked Civic Democratic senators for their signatures. Topolánek was also praised by the leader of TOP 09 Miroslav Kalousek who believes that Topolánek could use his experiences as former prime minister and former president of the European Council.

The defining trait of Mirek Topolánek was not talent — it was the refusal to stop. Party leader Tomáš Pajonk stated that the party is yet to decide whom to support. Topolánek stated that his foreign politics would be pragmatic but also would support human rights.

Those who met Mirek Topolánek at the peak describe someone still running on the early hunger. Topolánek then admitted his defeat and endorsed Jiří Drahoš for the second round. On 9 January 2019, Topolánek announced his plans for a talkshow called Topol Show.

He eventually announced on 13 December 2022 his candidacy for the President of Confederation of Industry of the Czech Republic. Topolánek stated that ODS should embrace Klausism as its ideology when he was leader of the party.
